neighbours.label: ' a' or ' an' as a split-off word start in a list of nouns, where a noun is expected: 'uncles, a|unts', 'corals, an|emones'
fire: Her grandparents, aunts and cousins came to the wedding.
Clams, anemones and crabs hide among the rocks.
I have brothers, aunts and nephews in Ohio.
Sponges, anemones and starfish cover the wall.
He sent cards to uncles, aunts and old friends.
Worms, anemones and shrimp filled the tank.
Our sisters, aunts and mothers cooked the meal.
Mussels, anemones and barnacles grow on the pier.
quiet: Her grandparents, cousins and nieces came to the wedding.
Clams, shrimp and crabs hide among the rocks.
I have brothers, sisters and nephews in Ohio.
Sponges, corals and starfish cover the wall.
He sent cards to uncles, cousins and old friends.
Worms, snails and shrimp filled the tank.
Our sisters, cousins and mothers cooked the meal.
Mussels, oysters and barnacles grow on the pier.

short: split-off a/an in a noun list
notes: Card: ' a' 6, ' at' 4, ' an' 4 of the top 32, each a split-off start of a longer word. Probes: ' a' before unts 0.68, ' an' before emones 0.39; 'to stay a|float' 0.08, ' in'|activity 0.11, ' at'|olls under 0.13, real articles 0.04. The tests are the two list cases only.
